cards.explanation: The answer is Titus. Paul writes, "I took Titus along also." (Galatians 2:1) So he went up to Jerusalem with Barnabas and Titus both. Titus comes up again in verse 3, friends.

The answer is those recognized as leaders. Paul says, "But I spoke privately to those recognized as leaders…" (Galatians 2:2) He sets before them the gospel he preaches among the Gentiles, and he speaks privately to the recognized leaders. I'd say it's like pulling the head baker aside for a quiet word about the batch.

The answer is that he was running in vain. Paul says he spoke to them "…for fear that I was running or had already run in vain." (Galatians 2:2) He's talking about his work spreading the gospel. I know that feeling about a batch I've been stamping for hours, friends.

The answer is False. Paul says, "…not even Titus, who was with me, was compelled to be circumcised, even though he was a Greek." (Galatians 2:3) The word is "compelled." Nobody forced it on Titus, friends.

The answer is to spy on their freedom in Christ. Paul says they came "…to spy on our freedom in Christ Jesus…" (Galatians 2:4) They didn't come as honest visitors, friends. They came in under false pretenses.

The word is enslave. Paul says they came in "…to spy on our freedom in Christ Jesus, in order to enslave us." (Galatians 2:4) Spying on freedom and then enslaving go together, and Paul names it plainly, bakers.
The answer is True. Paul says, "We did not give in to them for a moment…" (Galatians 2:5) Not even a moment, friends. They held firm the whole way through.

The answer is the truth of the gospel. Paul says they held firm "…so that the truth of the gospel would remain with you." (Galatians 2:5) The "you" is the Galatians, the very people reading his letter. He was holding that line for them, bakers.

The reason is that God does not show favoritism. Paul writes, "…whatever they were makes no difference to me; God does not show favoritism…" (Galatians 2:6) Their reputation isn't what Paul points to, friends. The reason he gives is that God does not show favoritism.
The answer is True. Paul says, "…those leaders added nothing to me." (Galatians 2:6) Think of showing someone your finished batch and hearing, "Nothing to add here."

The answer is circumcised. Paul says they saw "…that I had been entrusted to preach the gospel to the uncircumcised, just as Peter had been to the circumcised." (Galatians 2:7) Two men were given two groups, friends. It's the same gospel for both.

The answer is the same One who was at work in Peter. Paul says, "…the One who was at work in Peter’s apostleship to the circumcised was also at work in my apostleship to the Gentiles." (Galatians 2:8) Two different callings, bakers, and one and the same One at work in both.

The answer is True. Paul says, "recognizing the grace that I had been given, James, Cephas, and John…gave me and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship." (Galatians 2:9) They saw the grace on his life and welcomed him, friends.

The answer is the right hand of fellowship. Paul says they "…gave me and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship…" (Galatians 2:9) They did it recognizing the grace Paul had been given. It's a handshake, friends, and it says they're on the same team.

The request is to remember the poor. Paul says, "They only asked us to remember the poor…" (Galatians 2:10) A list that short even I could remember, and I'm the stamper who once lost track of a whole batch in the oven. Just one ask, friends, and it's about the poor.
The answer is False. Paul says remembering the poor was "…the very thing I was eager to do." (Galatians 2:10) He didn't need convincing, friends. The request matched what he already wanted to do.
